newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says deal will quadruple trade with Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Israel says deal will quadruple trade with Turkey.

text.p: Israel said on Monday that trade with Turkey could quadruple by the year 2000 under a free trade accord ratified by the Turkish parliament.
Israel's Foreign Ministry quoted economic observers as saying annual trade with Turkey -- Israel's main Middle East trading partner -- could approach $2 billion by then.
An Industry and Trade Ministry statement said that in 1996 Israel's trade with Turkey stood at around $450 million, of which $196 million was in exports and $252 million in imports.
Gabriela Cohen, deputy director of the Foreign Trade Administration, said once the deal took hold, "it will enable exports to Turkey to double within a few years".
The agreement, signed in March 1996, was given overwhelming approval in Ankara on Friday. Israel's trade administration promised to announce soon a precise date for lowering duties.
The accord envisages bringing Turkey's trade with Israel in harmony with Ankara's pledges to the European Union, with which it launched a customs union in 1996.
It also paves the way for Turkey to raise its trade with the United States, Canada and Central America through Israel, which has preferred trade ties with those countries.
Israel's Foreign Minister David Levy starts a two-day visit to Turkey on Tuesday, the first at a high level since both countries formed new governments last year.
Accompanied by Israeli businessmen, Levy will have talks with Turkish ministers and officials on investments and joint ventures in both countries.
But in Ankara on Monday, Israel's ambassador said Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan had spurned requests to meet Levy.
Ambassador Zvi Elpeleg said the reaction of the prime minister, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, flew in the face of assurances not to undermine growing ties.
